name: Atlas Linux desktop test schema
owner: BILLY-BADASS; MAC independently reviews evidence and owns release documentation

version_policy.scope: Ubuntu test operating system, explicitly clarified by Robert
version_policy.primary_environment: Latest generally available stable Ubuntu Desktop x86_64 at test start; exclude daily, beta, release-candidate and development images
version_policy.older_supported_releases: Separate explicitly identified compatibility cases; never label them latest stable
version_policy.atlas_target_policy: Keep the explicitly assigned Atlas candidate; latest-stable OS policy does not silently replace the product under test

atlas_target.family: screensaver-family Linux windowed X11/XWayland preview; not AtlasSOC standalone

required_environment_evidence: Official stable release lookup with timestamp and URL
Official ISO filename and verified SHA256; record any locally prepared installer separately
VM name/ID, x86_64 architecture, CPU, RAM, disk and NAT configuration
Installed /etc/os-release, running kernel, session type and XWayland availability
Installer ISO detached; guest root filesystem on virtual disk, not overlay/squashfs/tmpfs/casper
Official package indexes refreshed on installed guest; upgrades successful; no failed package configuration or required pending upgrades
Required reboot completed and kernel/update state checked after reboot
Clean powered-off baseline checkpoint ID, name and creation time verified

baseline_gate.unknown_or_failed_gate: BLOCKED; do not substitute a pre-install or partially updated snapshot

test_cases.record: Exact clone command, checked-out full revision, or full credential-free/TLS-preserving error
Verify specified hash, extract, run AppRun as normal guest user; dependency failures and package result
Map, labels/version, resize/maximize, country shading and expiry; screenshots without credentials/private telemetry
Real changing telemetry over validated TLS; accurate stale/offline behavior through guest disconnect/reconnect; no fake threats
Escape, close, process exit, relaunch and any delayed feed shutdown
Core tests and native Linux build at the assigned commit; record separately from published-package execution

limits: VM testing does not establish physical Linux hardware, idle/lock integration, GPU or multimonitor acceptance. Sending or receipt of a handoff is not execution or independent verification.
